call.summary: Hold / no new fundamental Buy at the $42.57 reference close. The illustrative base value is $48.60 (+14.2%), below a 30% analyst risk-margin hurdle. Its cash path still needs $26.08 billion of gross new borrowing plus $7.90 billion of gross equity, neither assured. This is a conditional scenario, not a firm fair-value target.
call.driver: Collect the stated customer deposits, finance installed equipment with actually closed project facilities, and retain attractive renewal pricing. The base requires $7.74 billion net hypothetical equity and 206.19 million financing shares, far beyond the 35 million-share September 30 ATM capacity.
call.strongest_objection: Management says project loans, prepayments and operating cash can cover the significant majority of capital needs; new contracts and paid-off GPUs may make this model too conservative. Conversely even 6.8 x EBITDA assumes 60% normalized unlevered cash conversion after maintenance replacement and tax, which is not established by disclosures.
call.falsifier: A Buy case needs confirmed collection of the approximately $9 billion deposits expected by roughly February 2027, sufficient closed project financing to replace the hypothetical debt draws, and a credible replacement-capex burden. Failure to obtain that funding or cash conversion invalidates the base rather than creating an automatic equity rescue.
call.rating_hurdle: A new fundamental Buy requires financing evidence and at least 30% base-case upside: at the current base cash path, a price no higher than about $37.39, or a defensible base value above $55.34 at the $42.57 reference price. Neither alone is sufficient while debt availability and mature-fleet replacement capex remain unverified.

gaps: No verified closed material financing after September 30 is added. SEC daily master indexes through November 25 show only Form 144/4 since November 17; November 26 was a US holiday. The IR index is partly rendered, so this is a bounded check rather than a guarantee of exhaustive issuer news.

Nine billion of prospective prepayments/deposits is a November 10 management expectation through roughly February 10,2027, not a confirmed subsequent cash balance. Collection, restriction, refund and recognition schedules are not publicly reconciled.

Quarterly 2027 principal repayment and capex timing are analyst allocations of annual totals. DDTL5.5 cash sweep and covenant-related accelerations can make actual payments earlier/higher than the smooth modeled schedule.

Future project borrowing well beyond disclosed undrawn capacity is required in every case. New-debt assumptions include refinancing and are not committed facilities. Failed loans or equity issuance invalidates the scenario; the calculator cannot guarantee funding.

The 35 million-share September 30 ATM capacity cannot fund the modeled downside/base equity gaps by itself. Any excess modeled issuance needs other registered offerings/authorizations and market demand; availability after September 30 is not independently confirmed.

No automatic conversion of out-of-money notes. Potential EPS-excluded options, warrants and unvested awards are not automatically added to basic shares; additional-share reserves are analyst estimates, not a fully reconciled vested/treasury-stock denominator.

Maintenance GPU replacement capex, recontracting retention and cash tax/capitalized-interest reconciliation remain insufficient for a defensible unconditional target. EBITDA cash-conversion anchors are illustrative and challenged explicitly; no implied peer multiple or fabricated consensus.

Enterprise valuation uses rent-expensed issuer-adjusted EBITDA. Operating lease liabilities are not also deducted as EV debt; operating rent is already in the cash operating margin. Finance leases are separate claims with cash payments in other uses. No NCI/preferred balance is reported; project cash leakage/claims could still differ.

Exact intraperiod shortfalls, accelerated sweeps, restricted draw proceeds, actual new-financing fees (1% assumed), asset-sale proceeds, interest income, and all local cash taxes are not independently forecast. Funding issuance is hypothetical at quarter/stub end, not assured liquidity throughout the interval.

Accounting interest scope: Note10 debt interest differs from the statement interest-expense total because other financing/lease items exist. Model rates estimate debt cash service, finance leases are separate, and forecast physical capex excludes capitalized financing interest. Exact future capitalized-interest and other cash-finance charges are not verified.

observed.unit: USD millions except shares millions, percentages, and power GW

customer_exposure.note: Anonymous A/B labels are period-specific: no named-customer attribution inferred. RPO is not added to revenue backlog. Net deferred-revenue movement is not gross customer cash receipts; reclassification is not an assumed refund.

conditional_funding.note: Facility availability is conditional on eligible collateral/contracts, covenants and draw windows, not available unrestricted cash. Revolver availability is a component, not additional to 5653.

recourse_and_covenants.note: DDTL4 has limited non-recourse carve-outs. Other DDTLs are parent-guaranteed, so project/SPV naming alone does not remove parent recourse. DDTL4 reserve covers forward debt service/opex and requires hedging; DDTL5.5 draws expire December 31,2026, amortization starts February 2027 and excess cash sweeps until principal 1300, with specified mandatory prepayments.

lease_scope.note: Future commitments are not present debt or all-current-year cash outlays. No double addition to modeled cash capex. DCSP gross 300 receivable/229 obligation is netted 71; neither gross side is added without restoring the other.

guidance.note: Exit ARR is December revenue annualized, not FY2027 revenue guidance. Guided capex is not assumed identical to cash purchases; Q4 cash capex is separately estimated.

conversion_audit.status: Illustrative matched-claim sensitivity; no entitlement, elected settlement or actual conversion forecast
notes: The retained-debt bull value is above nominal conversion strikes, but a target value is not a traded-price history. For the ordinary market-price route, holders need 20 of 30 trading days at 130% of the conversion price in the quarter ending before the conversion quarter. A single November 27 price does not establish eligibility.

Approximate 130% price thresholds are $140.14 for 2031, $155.48 for 2032 and $127.21 for 2033. The $137.40 retained-debt bull illustration exceeds only the 2033 threshold; even that needs the prior-quarter trading test. Other trading-price or corporate-event triggers may apply but are not assumed.

October 1,2027 physical-settlement illustrations assume the applicable September-quarter eligibility test was met and holders elected conversion; neither is known. Forced ordinary issuer redemption dates are later than target: December 5,2028 / October 8,2029 / April 5,2030 for 2031/2032/2033 respectively.

Every illustrated conversion removes the same principal from EV debt, adds only its contractual initial conversion shares, and saves its coupon from October 1 through target (58 days). No automatic principal-to-equity shortcut, retroactive interest saving or double count.

Gross physical-settlement illustrations give no capped-call recovery: strike/cap 2031 $107.80/$215.60,2032 $119.60/$230.00,2033 $97.85/$199.70. Early-unwind settlement, counterparties and make-whole rate changes are unknown. Capped calls could materially offset dilution, but their contractual eventual payoff is not assumed to be available cash in 2027.

illustrations.label: All three notes, hypothetical October 1 conversion

equity_capacity.note: The Q3 10-Q explicitly reports 35 million ATM shares remaining at September 30 and no ATM sales or collared forwards during the first nine months. Remaining capacity at the November 27 cutoff is unknown. This dated checkpoint is not proof of current issuance capacity or a guarantee that additional offerings can close.
